prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The bright foreground regions place the camera wearer’s hands and nearest metal bowl roughly 0.3–0.6 m away, with the newspaper, food pieces, and other bowls approximately 0.5–1.0 m away and separated from one another by about 0.1–0.4 m. The other person’s visible legs, feet, and occasional arm are farther away, roughly 1–2 m beyond or beside the work area, shifting from the upper left in frames 1–2 to the upper right in frames 3–5 as the viewpoint turns. The map clarifies foreground–background ordering and shows that the bowl and hands are within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, while the other person is generally beyond it; overlapping bright regions also reveal where the hands occlude the bowl and where the person is partly outside the image. Absolute metre estimates, person-facing direction, and apparent approach or retreat are unreliable because the depth is monocular, temporally inconsistent, and blurred around limbs and object boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The masks identify people and bowls as separate foreground regions, supporting a layout with the camera wearer’s hands at the lower centre, bowls and food directly ahead, and another person only partly visible near the upper edge. Across the frames, person-labelled regions move from the lower-left/centre toward the lower-right while another partial person region appears near the upper-right, consistent with viewpoint rotation rather than clear evidence of approach or retreat; the other person’s orientation and gaze cannot be determined reliably. The hand regions overlap the nearest bowl and lie within roughly 0.3–0.6 m of the camera, whereas the upper-edge person is approximately 1–2 m away and is clipped by the frame. The map is highly unreliable in places: large portions of the newspaper or work surface are labelled “bowl” or “remote,” several hands are labelled “person,” true objects are missed, and the masks do not provide dependable distance, facing direction, or separation between adjacent people.
descriptions.pose: The magenta skeletons consistently isolate the camera wearer’s hands near the lower centre of each frame, showing both hands close together above or around the nearest bowl and therefore within about 0.3–0.6 m and arm’s reach. Their image position shifts from left-of-centre in frame 1 to centre/right in later frames, while changes in finger and wrist geometry show hand turning and repositioning over the bowl more clearly than the dark RGB frames. No yellow body skeleton and no reliable skeleton for the other person appear, so the map provides almost no evidence about that person’s distance, facing direction, gaze, reach, or movement; their body remains partly out of view and sometimes occluded by the scene edge. Several hand skeletons are incomplete or distorted, especially in frame 4, and the map supplies neither metric depth nor dependable above/below or front/behind relationships beyond the hands’ 2-D overlap with the bowl.
